# @khalidsaidi/fallback-chain-js

Tiny fallback chains for JS/TS — try providers until one succeeds.

## Start here
- README.md: overview + quickstart + recipes
- llms-full.txt: full API + semantics + examples for LLMs/tools
- dist/index.js (ESM) / dist/index.cjs (CJS): the shipped implementation
- dist/index.d.ts / dist/index.d.cts: TypeScript types (full API surface)

## Concepts
- Candidates are lazy functions. We only call the next one if needed.
- Fallback can be triggered by:
  - a rejection/throw
  - or an “unacceptable” resolved value via options.accept(...)
- AbortSignal stops the entire chain.
- timeoutMs enforces per-attempt timeout via Promise.race (even if candidate ignores AbortSignal). Invalid timeoutMs (negative/NaN/non-number) throws TypeError instead of silently disabling the timeout.
- FallbackError (all candidates failed) carries .errors plus .named ([{ name?, error }]) and includes candidate names in its message when candidates are named.
- createFallbackChain(candidates, opts): stateful wrapper — failing candidates go on cooldown and are deprioritized (not skipped); success resets.
- fallbackStream(candidates, opts): streaming fallback — falls back only BEFORE the first chunk reaches the consumer; committed after that (mid-stream fallback is unsolvable UX).
